definition: Timorous means timid and easily frightened.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word timorous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know timorous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The timorous understudy rehearsed brilliantly and then hid in the wings whenever the director glanced her way.
Wary stops short of timorous — the wary keep sensible watch, while the timorous startle at shadows.
Cowardly goes further than timorous — the timorous feel fear everywhere, but the cowardly let it override duty.

Fearful describes fear felt in the moment — anyone can be fearful during turbulence and calm again on the ground. Timorous turns fear into temperament: a standing readiness to be frightened that shows up everywhere, about everything, real danger or none. Fearful is a passing state; timorous is a disposition.

Skittish means nervy and easily startled — said of horses and people alike, it points at jumpy reflexes, the sudden shy at a noise. Timorous runs deeper than reflex: a fearful temperament that shrinks back before any risk is even real. A skittish colt startles at the gate; a timorous one will not leave the stable.

'Cautious' weighs a risk and proceeds; timorous shrinks back before the risk is even real.
Timorous paints fearfulness as character — the mouse in the fable.
Everyday 'timid' or 'shy' is plainer.
